_comment: Constants the screen needs that no API endpoint returns, shipped as DATA
rather than computed in the browser.
D8 forbids the frontend deriving a number. It does not forbid the frontend
reading one: the difference that matters is whether a figure on the screen is
covered by a test in Python, and every figure in this file is. See
tests/test_web_frontend.py, which pins the CHSH bounds against math.sqrt and
the calibration table against the docstring of Detection.channel_error_rate
-- the same docstring the ~3050-test suite runs as a doctest. A number here
that drifts from its source fails the build.
Nothing in this file is a per-run quantity. Per-run figures come from

chsh.note: Reference lines on the CHSH chart. The classical bound is the CHSH inequality's own value and the Tsirelson bound is 2*sqrt(2); neither is a threshold this detector applies. Whether a link's Bell test failed is decided by the channel family in Python and appears in Signals -- never by comparing a bar to a line on a chart.

domain.note: The statistic's definitional range: four correlators, each in [-1, 1]. Used as the chart's axis so that no axis maximum is ever chosen from the data.

noise_null_calibration.source: Phase 5 experiment 'noise', 6 cells x 30 trials at L = 384, check_fraction 0.25. See docs/tables/noise.md for the provenance commit.
noise_null_calibration.regenerate: python tools/sweep.py run noise && python tools/sweep.py reduce noise
noise_null_calibration.what: Honest runs over a depolarising wire, scored against detect()'s default noiseless null (channel_error_rate = 0.0). The denominator is EVERY run at that level, not only the runs both verifiers accepted: at the design level 16 of the 60 verifier verdicts are rejections, because a link that noisy also moves the signature. Not a detection rate for any adversary: there is no adversary in any of these runs.
noise_null_calibration.with_true_rate_passed: 0/30 at every level when BOTH of detect()'s nulls are stated: the link's true matched-position error rate as channel_error_rate, AND the link's Werner strength as tolerated_depolarising. This table is the RATE family's. Correcting this null alone does not clear an honest noisy run.
noise_null_calibration.design_noise_note: 0.03125 is 2*s_a, the design noise level, and it fires on every run out of thirty. The honest baseline over a realistic link is the single most likely thing on this dashboard to be misread.
noise_null_calibration.second_null_note: That calibration is the RATE family. The CHANNEL family has its own null, tolerated_depolarising, also defaulting to a perfect resource, and stating only the first leaves an honest noisy run firing: measured over twelve seeds at L = 192, check_fraction = 0.25, link strength 0.03125 -- 12/12 detected with both nulls at zero, 12/12 with only channel_error_rate corrected, 0/12 with both stated. THE VERIFIERS DO NOT MOVE WITH THE NULLS AT ALL: their outcomes are the protocol's and the nulls are the detector's, and over those twelve seeds the pair of outcomes is identical under all three settings -- both accept on 7 seeds and Bob rejects the honest signature on 5, which is what a link at the design noise level does to a signature and is a separate fact from anything the detector said.

false_negative.note: There is no false-negative bound in this project and none can be derived from a transcript. Nothing on this screen may imply one: a quiet detector is not a proof that nothing happened.
